decision_scope: Whole AC83 clause set at current source; actual production Web + actual Electron IPC harness + Linux namespaces with explicit synthetic provider, plus canonical service race tests. Installed full Main, old clients, commercial provider account/quota, other OS and Mobile remain separate scopes.

clauses.clause: offline external participant, real login, sees assignment/transfer/information request/return/acceptance/invite/new comment/AI completed/failed/stopped
clauses.evidence: No workspaces/source membership; open+close client before events; logins unchanged; one fresh login (Web POST /auth/login, Electron password login into fresh profile). Six new kinds exactly once each. Invite seeded before first open; transferred (assignment and transfer) and comment_created from offline-handoff 2/2; 3 comment_created also present in final list.

clauses.clause: AI results notify only once confirmed
clauses.evidence: Proof held at 503 with zero result notices and proof_state=unknown; after natural proof: succeeded/failed/stopped, exited_proven. Canonical success/failure/missing/stopped/never_launched: 0 before proof, Stop intent not announced, null actor.

clauses.clause: opens issue through the account workbench
clauses.evidence: Popover title link opens heading on both clients; #run-<UUID> focuses Termination confirmed records; ai_failed shows No business result recorded / Partial recording, API business_outcome null and recording partial.

clauses.clause: actor receives no notice for own action
clauses.evidence: Per workflow event the actor has 0 notices for that event_seq; the other participant and H have 1 each. Offline-handoff: creator gets none for own invite/assignment; H unchanged after own transfer-back. Canonical invite excludes actor.

clauses.clause: read/archive do not change handling or authority
clauses.evidence: 12 real UI POSTs return 200; issue snapshot, participating/current workbench unchanged after each; archive removes row only.

clauses.clause: removed participant gets only a content-free removal notice and cannot open via old notices
clauses.evidence: Exactly one added removed notice (10 to 11); all items issue_title null, can_open false, source_id null, no run_id; account WS access_changed with ID/version-only keys; old result href denied on Web and Electron; issue and old run-records URLs 404; participating list empty; creator keeps the issue.

clauses.clause: source-member participant not duplicated in source inbox; external participant creates no source inbox/subscriber
clauses.evidence: Creator source membership 1 and participant; H membership 0; inbox_item=0 and issue_subscriber=0 at four checkpoints; canonical workspace-wide and recipient-specific inbox 0, subscribers 0.

clauses.clause: notification delivery failure does not affect business operation
clauses.evidence: Persistence failure rolls back atomically (InformationRequestRequiredWritesRollback/INSERT_INTO_collaboration_notification; ResultNotificationRollbackAndConcurrentReplay). Post-commit publisher failure keeps committed data with pending outbox, stable-identity retry and no private payload (RealtimeOutboxRetriesWithoutPrivatePayloads, RealtimeRetainsFailedSourceInvalidation).

Original-key workflow replay: identical receipt, issue and notifications. Original natural proof bytes unchanged across retries; second replay returns 200 with identical issue/notice. Canonical concurrent replay gives exactly 2 recipients, not recomputed for later participant; outbox redelivery count stays 1. Offline-handoff covers invite/transfer replay.

nonblocking_limitations: Electron login-after-offline is a real password API login into a fresh isolated profile, not login-page UX or installed full Main.
Assignment and transfer share server kind transferred; no UI assertion covers creator receipt of H's transfer-back; same fanout is shown for information_requested and canonically for invite.
Comment self-exclusion is not reasserted here; relies on current AC90/91/97 retain_passed, not re-reviewed.
Browser source-isolation zero counts have no positive control; canonical tests and parent design.md:214 own that rule.
Canonical post-commit publisher failure uses a creation event; the generic outbox path is not repeated for every AC83 kind.
Browser ai_failed is natural missing-outcome/partial recording, not commercial model failure; canonical failure subtest covers explicit business failure.
Listener/build identity accepted from root preflight; not probed by this review.
